Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

complete verb

finish (a task)

also finish a job, get done, finish off, completion, get it over and done with, get it over with, complete a year, finish writing, put the finishing touch to, finishing touch

classical

Cato Agr. 2.1: satisne temperī opera sient cōnfecta
Verg. G. 2.541: sed nōs immēnsum spatiīs cōnfēcimus aequor
Traupman 294
Traupman 315

cōnficiō, cōnficere, cōnfēcī, cōnfectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive

complete, finish, get done

Other words

  • perficiō, perficere, perfēcī, perfectum — complete, carry through, finish properly

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Liv. 1.55.1: patrem vōvisse, fīlium perfēcisse; Traupman 33, 364: perficere pēnsum; īnstā, perfice!

    Of finishing a thing well: Lewis & Short sets absolvere apart from it, as “without denoting intrinsic excellence, like perficere”.

  • absolvō, absolvere, absolvī, absolūtum — finish off, get done

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Traupman 99, 315, 320: negōtium absolvere; Traupman 99: negōtium absolvere; Traupman 320

    Lewis & Short: “to bring a work to a close, to complete, finish”, probably from taking a finished web off the loom.

Examples

  • vīlicum vocet, roget quid operis siet factum, quid restet, satisne temperī opera sient cōnfecta, possitne quae reliqua sient cōnficere

    Let him call the farm manager and ask what work has been done, what is left, whether the jobs were finished in good time, and whether he can finish what remains.Cato Agr. 2.1

  • aliud est properāre, aliud festīnāre. quī ūnum quid mātūrē trānsigit, is properat; quī multa simul incipit neque perficit, is festīnat

    Hurrying is one thing, rushing another: whoever finishes one thing promptly is hurrying; whoever starts many things at once and finishes none is rushing.Gell. 16.14.2 (Cato)

  • Tarquiniōs rēgēs ambōs patrem vōvisse, fīlium perfēcisse

    both Tarquin kings: the father vowed it, the son completed itLiv. 1.55.1

  • annum explēre

    to complete a yearTraupman 294

  • ultimam manum afferre

    to put the finishing touch toTraupman 315

  • carmen nōndum recēpit ultimam manum

    the poem has not yet had its finishing touchPetr. 118 (Lewis & Short s.v. manus)

  • negōtium absolvere

    to get the business over and done withTraupman 320

See also achieve, job, eat up, manage.
